pages.text: $(l)A machine does not turn Look at its shaft with goggles.$() No speed means nothing reaches it: check every shaft and cogwheel on the way. If the network is $(item)overstressed$(), everything on it stops: add a source or remove consumers.

Some machines also need a minimum speed: a single air intake needs 40 RPM, the surface scanner 64 RPM.$(br2)$(l)A vat attachment does nothing$()$(br)See the vat page: one stopped machine on a vat blocks every recipe, so give it rotation or power, or take it off.

$(l)Electricity destroys blocks Every electrical block has a $(item)maximum voltage$() (1000 V for most of them) and some have a maximum current.$() Above it for a moment, the block $(item)is destroyed and drops nothing$(). The goggles and the multimeter warn first with $(item)Approaching Overvoltage$() or $(item)Approaching Overcurrent$() at 80% of the limit.
Lower the voltage with a transformer or a resistor before it reaches small machines, and use cables rated for the current.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
